title: MCPStdioClient never drains subprocess stderr
description: start() creates the subprocess with stderr=PIPE but nothing ever reads it. A chatty MCP server fills the pipe buffer and deadlocks the bridge. Either drain stderr into the logger or stop piping it.
close_reason: Background stderr drain task added in 77b3a68 with a reproducing regression test

title: MCPStdioClient drops server-initiated requests and notifications
description: _read_response discards any message whose id does not match the pending request id. MCP servers can call back into the client (sampling/createMessage, roots/list, elicitation/create) and send notifications; those are silently dropped. Blocks real bidirectional MCP client support.
close_reason: Background read loop routes responses, server requests, and notifications in 7114a96

title: Support runtime-configured MCP servers via session/new mcpServers
description: python-acp currently binds ONE MCP server at startup via --mcp-command in cli.py, shared by all WebSocket clients. ACP v1 has the client pass mcpServers in session/new, making the agent an MCP client to N per-session servers. Needs a connection registry keyed by session, replacing the single MCPStdioClient held by ACPWebSocketBridge.

title: Preserve MCP error codes and tool isError through the bridge
description: Two failure signals are flattened today. (1) A JSON-RPC error from the MCP server becomes MCPProtocolError(str(error)), losing the code, and ws_bridge maps every one to -32603 -- a server's -32601 and -32602 are indistinguishable to a WebSocket client. (2) A tool that fails returns a SUCCESSFUL result with isError: true; nothing inspects it (ws_bridge.py:119, :235) so the client sees ok: true. Both are wire-contract changes -- see the acp-protocol skill.

title: Honor nextCursor pagination in the MCP list wrappers
description: list_tools, list_prompts, and list_resources read only the first page of the result and drop nextCursor. Against a paginated MCP server the bridge silently reports a partial list with no error. Loop until nextCursor is absent.

title: Declare client capabilities in the MCP initialize request
description: initialize sends capabilities: {} so no conforming MCP server will ever send roots/list, elicitation/create, or sampling/createMessage -- even though _handle_server_request is wired to route them to on_server_request. Declare the capabilities we can actually answer (elicitation is the one that maps onto ACP session/request_permission; roots is plausible from session cwd/additionalDirectories; sampling must NOT be declared, there is no LLM in this runtime). Elicitation requires bumping the pinned protocol version to 2025-06-18.

title: Negotiate the MCP protocolVersion instead of ignoring the server's answer
description: MCPStdioClient.initialize sends protocolVersion 2024-11-05 and never reads the version the server returns. Per the MCP lifecycle spec a server that does not support the requested version MUST reply with one it does support, and the client SHOULD disconnect if that version is unusable. Today the handshake appears to succeed and the mismatch surfaces later as confusing failures. Compare the returned protocolVersion against what was sent and fail loudly.

title: Add an mcp-protocol skill covering the embedded MCP subprocess
description: python-acp embeds an MCP server subprocess (MCPStdioClient) but has no skill documenting the MCP wire protocol it speaks. The acp-protocol skill covers the WebSocket side only. Add a project skill covering the MCP stdio transport rules, the initialize/initialized lifecycle, capability negotiation, the client/server primitive surface, and the places where mcp_stdio.py currently diverges from the spec.
close_reason: Skill written to .claude/skills/mcp-protocol/{SKILL.md,spec-versions.md}; conventions bullet added to CLAUDE.md and mirrored to AGENTS.md; mcp_stdio.md links it; six divergences filed as pyacp-z3y/pb7/x8l/a92/ua1/k5w

title: Serialize-per-request lock blocks concurrent MCP calls
description: MCPStdioClient.request holds self._lock across both write and read, so every call is fully serialized with no pipelining. Acceptable for one server; becomes a bottleneck once multiple sessions and servers share the runtime.
close_reason: Resolved as a consequence of 7114a96: the write lock no longer spans the reply wait, so requests pipeline. Covered by test_concurrent_requests_are_all_answered

title: Send notifications/cancelled when an MCP request times out
description: request() raises MCPProtocolError after request_timeout but sends nothing to the server, which keeps working on a reply nobody will read. The spec's remedy is a notifications/cancelled carrying the requestId. Needs a mock_mcp_server.py branch that reports what it received.

title: Close the subprocess stdin before SIGTERM in MCPStdioClient.stop
description: The MCP stdio shutdown sequence is: close the server's stdin, wait for exit, SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL. stop() starts at terminate(), so servers that exit cleanly on EOF get signalled instead of shutting down normally.
